description: INGRID is the 1024x1024 HAWAII near-infrared camera for 0.8-2.5 micron imaging on the William Herschel Telescope (WHT).
short_description: WHT INGRID near-IR camera filters, warm and cold scans
facility_description: The William Herschel Telescope (WHT) is a 4.2-meter optical/near-infrared telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma, operated by the Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes (ING).
notes: INGRID filter-only scans; warm laboratory measurements and cold estimates remain distinct named variants. The ING filter pages (www.ing.iac.es) did not respond during verification, so no links are kept. DetectorType photon, DetectorTypeSource inferred (2026-10-26): no owner states the integration convention for the curve file, but the ING files are filter %T scans ('Filter Brg Temp=77K', https://www.ing.iac.es/Astronomy/instruments/ingrid_new/filter/brg.cold.trans.html), and INGRID 'uses a 1k x 1k HAWAII detector' (https://www.ing.iac.es/Astronomy/instruments/ingrid_new/), so the curves integrate as photon counters. The source is 'inferred' because this rests on the published curve content and the documented detector, not on an explicit owner statement.

BRG_WARM.DetectorType_note: SVO's WHT/INGRID.Brg_w (captured 2023-03-23) is the same array as NJM's (SVO/NJM ratio 1.000 wherever both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ING's filter %T scans and INGRID's HAWAII photon-counting detector (see the instrument notes).
BRG_WARM.Comments: SVO match set to WHT/INGRID.Brg_w (2026-10-26). It had no SVO match. SVO's WHT/INGRID.Brg_w (captured 2023-03-23) is the same array as NJM's (SVO/NJM ratio 1.000 wherever both exceed 5 % of peak).

FEII_COLD.DetectorType_note: SVO's WHT/INGRID.FeII (captured 2023-03-26) is the same curve as NJM's within resampling (SVO/NJM ratio 0.999-1.002 where both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ING's filter %T scans and INGRID's HAWAII photon-counting detector (see the instrument notes).

FEII_WARM.Comments:
Temp=77K, tilted 5 deg
calculated from data at room temperature and O deg incidence SVO match set to WHT/INGRID.FeII_w (2026-10-26). It had been matched by name and pivot to WHT/INGRID.FeII, a spectrally shifted scan (the array of NJM's FEII_COLD). SVO lists this ID but no capture is archived yet; the warm records Jcont_w, Kcont_w and Pab_w are each identical to NJM's matching WARM band, so FeII_w is the expected counterpart (unverified until harvested).
